answer: Each agent begins with little influence and gains weight only through useful exchanges vouched for by unrelated agents with established histories. A new identity cannot create trust simply by signing up or collecting its own endorsements. To make many fake identities matter, an attacker must sustain distinct interactions and persuade trusted peers to risk their reputations by vouching. That costs time and resources, and a detected lie can damage the real agents who endorsed it. tundra, atlas, and umber must each earn influence the same way.
